title: Listen before you bring your agenda
header_line: My analysis of one book on an entrepreneur's life. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: Do you go into a negotiation to listen, or to deliver your agenda?

I said: I don't want to be political. I'm very careful when I say things. It is not always what you read and see on the news. There are always two sides to the coin. In the end I attribute a lot of these problems to a lack of cultural sensitivity.
A student said: it is a balancing act, and something that has played out through history, in several places.

I said that this will come into play when they talk about negotiations. They will hold two or three classes at least on negotiation. When you negotiate on behalf of a country, you really have to be a good listener.

Some of the people with enormous responsibilities come with an agenda, I said. It is kind of the structure of the military: you have a mission and you are very linear about what you are supposed to accomplish. That training is a double-edged sword. You know exactly what your objective is, but it doesn't always work like that. It is not black and white.

Imagine the responsibility of someone in a foreign country who is interpreting information and bringing it back to the capital, I said. A student said: it is a good game of telephone, and the agendas tend to persevere.
What do you listen for first, before you bring your agenda?

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write the last negotiation you went into with an agenda.
Write what you would have heard if you had listened first.
Write how information changes as it passes from person to person in your work.
Write what cultural differences you have had to learn.
Write the first question you will ask next time.

check.q: What did I attribute a lot of these problems to?
What did I say you have to be when negotiating for a country?
What did I call training that gives you a linear mission?

recap: Listen before you bring your agenda. Remember that information changes as it travels.
